sentences.text: THIS BAIL APPLICATION HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 11.03.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:

B.A.No.1485/2025 3  2025:KER:20697  P.V.KUNHIKRISHNAN, J  --------------------------------
 B.A.No.1485 of 2025  -------------------------------
 Dated this the 11th day of March, 2025  ORDER This Bail Application is filed under Section 482 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.

2. The petitioners are accused in Crime No.76/2025 on the files of the Tanur Police Station,
Malappuram district.

The offences alleged against the petitioner are under Sections 342, 376(2)(n)
of the Indian Penal Code and Section 75 of the Juvenile Justice Act and Section 6 r/w Section 5(1)
and 17 of the POCSO Act, 2012.
3. The prosecution case is that the 1st petitioner committed rape on the minor girl and other accused abetted the 1st petitioner and thereby the the accused committed the above offences.
4. Heard counsel for the petitioners and the Public Prosecutor.
5. The learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the allegations against the petitioners are false.
It is submitted that the engagement between the 1 st petitioner and the defacto complainant is over and subsequently, she filed the above complaint.
It is submitted that the petitioners are ready to abide 2025:KER:20697 by any conditions that may be imposed by this Court.
6. The learned Public Prosecutor opposed the bail application.
7. This Court considered the contentions of the petitioners and the respondents.
This Court also perused the first information statement.

After going through the first information statement, I am of the considered opinion that the 1 st and 2nd petitioners are not entitled for bail under Section 482 of Mohammed Rasal.C vs State Of Kerala on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119547451/

sentences.text: the BNSS.
Considering the fact and circumstances of the case, the 3 rd petitioner can be granted bail.
Therefore, the bail application of the 1st and 2nd petitioners are dismissed.
The bail application of the 3rd petitioner is allowed with stringent conditions.

Therefore, this bail application is allowed in part with the following directions:
1. The 3rd petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer within two weeks from today and shall undergo interrogation.

2. After interrogation, if the Investigating Officer propose to arrest the 3rd petitioner he shall be released on bail on executing a bond for a sum of Rs.50,000/-(Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the arresting officer 2025:KER:20697 concerned.
3. The 3rd petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer for interrogation as and when required.

The 3rd petitioner shall co- operate with the investigation and shall not, directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer.
4.
The 3rd petitioner shall not leave India without permission of the jurisdictional Court.
5. The petitioners shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

6. Needless to mention, it would be well within the powers of the investigating officer to investigate the matter and, if necessary, to effect recoveries on the information, if any, given by the 3rd petitioner even while the 3rd petitioner are on bail as laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sushila Aggarwal 2025:KER:20697 v. State (NCT of Delhi) and another [2020 (1) KHC 663].
7.
